results.name: From Endpoint to Funhouse: Changes in Ransomware Families and Kimsuky-Related Distribution Cases
results.description: A North Korean threat actor distributed Funhouse ransomware through malicious Korean-language documents disguised as resumes. Funhouse is a variant of the previously observed Endpoint ransomware. The attack chain involves multi-stage scripts including Batch, VBS, and PowerShell, leading to Quasar RAT installation before deploying the final ransomware payload. The campaign shares significant similarities with earlier Kimsuky Endpoint ransomware operations from early 2026, including identical mutex values, similar batch file structures, and comparable Quasar RAT configurations. The ransomware maintains key characteristics of the Endpoint family while updating encryption extensions, contact information, and C2 infrastructure. A notable shift involves using HWP documents instead of LNK files as initial infection vectors.

results.name: Analysis of Wpcdoor Attack Case Distributed Through Domestic DVR Management Software
results.description: A South Korean company's DVR management software (CMS) was exploited to distribute the Wpcdoor backdoor malware. The attack chain begins when CMS.exe installs rs.win32.exe along with a malicious IPHLPAPI.DLL file that loads via DLL side-loading. This first-stage downloader retrieves WpcMon.exe and samcli.dll, which acts as a second-stage downloader executing the Wpcdoor backdoor in memory. Wpcdoor exfiltrates system information including screenshots, clipboard data, browser credentials, wallet extension data, and supports various commands for remote control. The backdoor targets cryptocurrency wallets including MetaMask, Coinbase, and Phantom. The attacker, designated as Larva-26013, continues to deploy Wpcdoor through multiple attack vectors beyond the DVR software compromise.

results.name: Beyond the clipboard: The evolving tradecraft of ClickFix
results.description: Threat actors continue to evolve ClickFix tactics, moving beyond simple clipboard-based social engineering to more sophisticated attack chains. Recent campaigns leverage malvertising through typosquatting, SEO poisoning, and compromised websites to deliver fake verification prompts. These attacks now employ elaborate PowerShell scripts with animated progress bars to mimic legitimate security checks. Observed payloads include Node.js-based RATs like DuskDesk, lateral movement techniques targeting domain controllers via WinRM and SSH tunnels, and steganographic delivery chains hiding executables within PNG files. Some campaigns utilize browser-cache-seeded attacks that detect the victim's browser and retrieve staged payloads from cached files. Defense requires user training to recognize social engineering, application control policies, and behavioral monitoring for suspicious command execution patterns and persistence mechanisms.

results.name: A New ESXi Implant Linked to Settra Ransomware
results.description: GhostFrame is a previously undocumented post-exploitation framework enabling extensive control over compromised VMware ESXi environments. After root-level access is obtained, it provides a unified interface for accessing virtual machines, harvesting credentials, executing commands, and pivoting into victim networks. The framework operates from the virtualization layer, allowing attackers to control multiple VMs from a single compromised ESXi host. TAG-218, whose operations overlap with Settra ransomware, has been observed deploying GhostFrame following compromise of VPN appliances across the US and Europe. The implant establishes persistence, disables security controls, uses distinctive C2 communications across multiple ports, and integrates credential harvesting tools including VMkatz. This demonstrates how compromised hypervisors serve as centralized platforms for post-exploitation activities across virtualized environments.

results.name: Dark Web Profile: CyberXero
results.description: CyberXero is a Russian-speaking, financially motivated Initial Access Broker operating on Dark Web forums, conducting two parallel operations: a global mass-exploitation campaign targeting WordPress, Magento and e-commerce platforms, and a directed campaign focused on Ukrainian energy and utilities organizations. The actor distinguishes itself through AI augmentation, deploying 51 specialized Claude Code agents and PentAGI integrated with Cobalt Strike. Active since July 2026, CyberXero generates revenue through access brokering, payment data theft, and cryptocurrency payments. Over 40 organizations across Ukraine, Poland, China, Pakistan and the Netherlands have been affected, with more than 628,000 personal records exfiltrated and 429 WordPress administration panels compromised. The actor weaponizes vulnerabilities within 30 days and employs sophisticated techniques including SQL injection, PHP deserialization, and lateral movement tactics.

results.name: Not All That Glitters Is Gold: Tracking CopperDragon's Sparrow Framework Around the Globe
results.description: Over the past year, researchers investigated intrusion campaigns targeting high-profile organizations across Latin America, Asia, and Europe. These initially appeared independent but were linked through shared tools and infrastructure to the Sparrow malware ecosystem. CopperDragon is tracked as a digital quartermaster supporting China-nexus threat actors using the Sparrow cross-platform framework. Three distinct activity clusters were identified: SilentDelivery using watering-hole attacks with fake certificate warnings deploying SquadC backdoor; OceanGate targeting government and critical infrastructure with AnnobinDoor and SparrowShell backdoors; and DarkWire focusing on telecommunications and government entities using CopperDoor and CopperDNS backdoors. Operations employed sophisticated techniques including kernel rootkits, passive backdoors with packet interception, trojanized SSH tools, and extensive credential harvesting across Linux and Windows environments.

results.name: The Cold Chain on Fire: Unpatched Danfoss controllers exploited
results.description: Between October and November 2026, hundreds of supermarkets across France and over a dozen European countries suffered cyberattacks targeting unpatched Danfoss refrigeration controllers directly exposed to the internet. Attackers modified temperature settings and defrost cycles, causing food spoilage worth tens of millions of euros. The exploitation leveraged outdated firmware vulnerabilities, including authentication bypass flaws, without requiring sophisticated code execution capabilities. French authorities attributed the operations to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps unit "Shahid Kaveh," linked to CyberAveng3rs, known for previous attacks on U.S. critical infrastructure. The incidents demonstrate how exposed industrial control systems enable disruptive attacks and how generative AI can accelerate exploit development for ICS devices.

results.name: Inside an AhsayCBS Intrusion: Hidden Webshells, a CryptoMiner, and a C2 Implant
results.description: Between October 8 and 11, 2026, threat actors exploited authentication bypass and remote code execution vulnerabilities in AhsayCBS backup management software to compromise multiple servers. The intrusion involved deploying five distinct webshell families with varying capabilities, including command execution, file operations, and encrypted payload loaders hidden in PNG images. Attackers installed two XMRig cryptocurrency miners with scheduled task persistence, staged tunneling tools, and deployed a custom Python-based implant with environmental keying that communicated with command-and-control infrastructure. The operators created Microsoft Defender exclusions, accessed backup credentials through Veeam database queries, and specifically targeted backup infrastructure to potentially access stored credentials for hypervisors and domain accounts. The sophisticated multi-stage attack demonstrated significant operational patience beyond typical smash-and-grab cryptomining campaigns.

results.name: Trusted by Default: Qubole Cross-Account Access Abused in the Wild
results.description: A threat actor exploited IAM credentials from Qubole's AWS account (805246085872) to assume integration roles in customer environments between October 14 and October 26, 2026. The attacker used two IAM users and multiple VPN addresses to gain access, then conducted extensive reconnaissance across affected AWS accounts. Activities included enumerating storage, databases, and identity resources, harvesting credentials from Lambda environment variables, Secrets Manager, and SSM Parameter Store, and validating discovered credentials using TruffleHog. The actor exfiltrated data from S3 buckets opportunistically, downloading whatever each assumed role could access. A suspicious bootable Linux ISO image was also identified, designed for remote deployment and system reconnaissance. The campaign appears opportunistic rather than state-sponsored, exploiting trusted cross-account relationships that remained active despite many integrations being unused.

results.name: On the hunt for ARTEX: understanding agentic attacks in AWS environments
results.description: In October 2026, an AI-native penetration framework called ARTEX was observed conducting attacks against AWS environments, primarily targeting financial data. ARTEX operates through LLM agents that autonomously plan and execute attacks based on operator-defined objectives. Observed activity included exploitation of compromised long-term IAM access keys to search CloudWatch logs for financial information, file paths, and secrets. Additionally, attackers abused public Amazon Cognito user pools through anonymous sign-ups, token collection, and AWS account enumeration. Datadog identified hundreds of internet-exposed ARTEX consoles, often in Mandarin and hosted in Singapore and Hong Kong. The framework has been linked to China-aligned threat actor Storm-0940 and demonstrates sophisticated post-exploitation capabilities including automated resource discovery and credential harvesting across cloud environments.
